title: Quiet Oncall Ramp: adaptive alert-sampling + telemetry-sampler CLI
author: Evan Brooks
description:
Motivation: Pager fatigue from noisy non-actionable alerts continues to erode on-call effectiveness. This change introduces the 'Quiet Oncall Ramp' (QOR) pattern: adaptive sampling of telemetry and alert footprints to reduce on-call wakeups while preserving high-fidelity diagnostics for triage.

What this PR does: Adds a new lightweight service + CLI (qorctl) that periodically samples low-priority signals, attaches compact telemetry digests to alerts, and progressively reduces wake probability for noisy signals based on a configurable sampling policy. It also ships a runbook suggester that uses the sampled digest to propose short mitigation steps (e.g. restart, throttle, failover) and a safe revert plan.

Design notes: The sampler keeps a sliding-window histogram of alert fingerprints and associated aggregated traces/metrics (compact rollups only — no full traces). Sampling decisions are policy-driven: start at 100% for new fingerprints, decay to a floor (default 1%) once fingerprint noise is confirmed. Alerts with high severity or matching suppression-exempt labels bypass sampling. The runbook suggester uses the digest to match heuristics and returns ranked suggestions with confidence scores.

Compatibility: Integrates with existing incident-bot alert enrichment hooks and SLO Toolkit's telemetry backfills. The CLI has a dry-run mode and a safe-mode that only annotates alerts (no suppression).

Rollout plan: Canary to 1% of teams for two weeks (feature gate), monitor missed-action metric, then 10%/50%/100% ramp. Auto-rollback if missed-action increases > 3x baseline or mean time to ack increases by > 25%.

Testing: unit tests for policy evaluation, lightweight integration tests that exercise the enrichment API and CLI, local smoke runs with synthetic noisy signals. CI includes a synthetic-noise regression job to detect sampling regressions.

Related: Linear ENG-10450 (oncall fatigue metrics), ENG-10612 (alert fingerprinting improvements).

review_comments: Maya Patel (requested changes): The default policy floor feels aggressive for multi-tenant clusters — can we make the floor configurable per-namespace and add a recommended profile for platform-owned services?
Evan Brooks (author): Added namespace-scoped override and a 'platform' profile in examples/policies. Also added a note in rollout checklist to coordinate with platform SLA owners.
Dmitri Ivanov (nit): In sampler.go's histogram serialization, prefer fixed-width buckets to avoid noisy cardinality growth. (resolved in commit 'fix(hist): use fixed buckets')
Priya Ramesh (approved): Verified canary behavior locally and ran the synthetic-noise regression; LGTM after minor doc tweak.
release_notes: Adds Quiet Oncall Ramp (QOR): adaptive alert sampling, telemetry-digest enrichment, qorctl CLI, and runbook suggester. Can be enabled per-namespace; default policy included. Backwards-compatible, disabled by default.
notes_on_deployment: Feature gated; requires incident-bot 2.4 enrichment hook. Ops runbook included in docs/quiet-oncall-ramp.md. Monitor 'qor.missed_action_rate' and 'qor.sampled_alert_count' after rollout.
